cross_disciplinary_pairing.description: The diagnosis is not limited to a generic agronomic text rephrasing: the water stress data comes from extracting a scientific remote-sensing dataset (healthy/stressed bounding boxes on Red/NIR multispectral imagery, Butte et al. 2021), and the NDVI = (NIR-Red)/(NIR+Red) computation is reproduced directly on the raw channels (scripts/compute_ndvi.py, correlation r=0.89 with the annotations). The local LLM then only interprets these already-quantified measurements.

test_prompts.prompt: You are an agronomic assistant helping a field operator interpret the drone mission history for a potato plot. You never receive an image, only figures that are already computed, and you never invent a figure absent from the provided context. Full history of plot PARC-01, oldest to most recent: 06/01 → 18.2% stressed zones (2/11); 07/05 → 33.3% (4/12); 08/15 (current mission) → 54.5% (6/11). Threshold grid: 0-15% Normal, 15-35% Vigilance, 35-60% Alert, above 60% Critical. Write a clear diagnosis, in English, that explicitly describes the trajectory across the 3 missions (not just the gap with the latest measurement), then end with a concrete, actionable recommendation that accounts for this dynamic.

Same context: agronomic assistant interpreting the results of a drone mission on a potato plot, never inventing a figure absent from the context. Mission data: current water stress 77.8% of zones (7 stressed zones out of 9), up 20.7 points from the previous mission (57.1%, recorded during a prolonged heat wave). Threshold grid: 0-15% Normal, 15-35% Vigilance, 35-60% Alert, above 60% Critical. Write a clear diagnosis, in English, ending with a concrete, quantified, actionable recommendation (number of zones to prioritize, intervention timeframe in hours) suited to a critical level.
